title: St. Edmund School Modernization, 11712 - 130 Avenue, Edmonton (1954 school; Edmonton Catholic School Division)
jurisdiction: City of Edmonton, Alberta (owner: Edmonton Catholic School Division; AHJ not stated in source)

facts.text: Location 11712 - 130 Avenue, Edmonton; owner/developer Edmonton Catholic School Division; architect ACI Architects Inc.; structural consultant RJC Engineers; mechanical consultant Arrow Engineering Inc.; electrical consultant AECOM Engineering Inc.; general contractor Whitson Contracting Ltd.
Building dates from 1954; total size 4,814 m2 main and 3,195 m2 second floor; total cost $14.9 million.
facts.locator: PDF p.1, sidebar TOTAL SIZE and TOTAL COST; lede

facts.text: Scope included replacement of the roof, mechanical and electrical systems, parking, utility connections and landscaping. Quoted project manager: 'a complete gut and refurbish ... the only thing that stayed were the foundations and walls.'
facts.locator: PDF p.1, paragraph quoting Jade Sawchuk

facts.text: Corridors were widened for accessibility and windows were replaced for energy efficiency (quoted project manager).
facts.locator: PDF p.1, paragraph beginning 'Sawchuk adds that all the corridors'

facts.text: The original building was wood frame. The quoted team said they added 'construction parameters to make the building as fire proof as possible' and 're-boarded the entire building with an additional layer of drywall to meet the fire rating.' The speaker is not named in the text.
facts.locator: PDF p.1, unattributed quotation after the 'three different structural systems' sentence

facts.text: The building had three structural systems: wood frame; concrete block, given 'a fairly extensive gut and redo'; and post-and-beam steel with concrete floors.

In the CTS lab the planned rooftop air handling unit was 'too heavy for the roof structure'; the article describes structural piles and beams for support and new upgrades that can 'roughly support four 70-ton tanks in lieu of the new AHU and associated snow loads.'
facts.locator: PDF p.1, paragraphs quoting Connor Whitson and following narrative

facts.text: Existing sewer utilities were '20-feet below slab, plugged, or partially collapsed'; new services were tunnelled in and connected over summer to keep the school operating.
facts.locator: PDF p.1, paragraph quoting Connor Whitson

facts.text: Work proceeded with the school open. Phasing 'had to be adjusted three times' (Kevin Osborne, ACI); over 40 percent of the school was renovated in the four summer months, which the article says was 15 percent of the schedule (Connor Whitson).
facts.locator: PDF p.1, quotations from Osborne and Whitson near the end of the article
